articles.headline: Takeaways: LeBron at center?! Why the 76ers had to get creative on opening night
articles.description: Brian Windhorst examines a surprising shift for LeBron, plus more takeaways from the NBA's season-opening tripleheader.
articles.headlineJa: 考察：レブロンがセンターに？！なぜ76ersは開幕戦で独創的な策を講じる必要があったのか
articles.descriptionJa: ブライアン・ウィンドホーストが、レブロンの驚くべき役割の変化や、NBA開幕3試合におけるその他の注目点を解説する。
articles.body:
Consider Oct. 21, 2025: NBA opening night inside Crypto.com Arena.

A 40-year-old LeBron James, who hadn't missed a season opener in his 23-year career, is watching from the bench with a nagging sciatica that would push his season debut -- in his final year under contract with the Los Angeles Lakers -- to mid-November.

Which of the following would've been the most surprising if you had a crystal ball (and chose NBA opening night 2026) to see into the future:

James, now 41, still playing at a high level,

for the Philadelphia 76ers,

at ... center?

James' distaste for playing defensive center spans decades because of the wear and tear. But his move there at times Tuesday night, albeit alongside big man Joel Embiid for much of it, should be one of the biggest takeaways from the 76ers' 106-100 win at Madison Square Garden.

Not only did he play backup center at times Tuesday night, but there were numerous possessions where James defended Knicks center Karl-Anthony Towns, with Embiid sliding to guard Josh Hart. It enabled the 76ers to better defend Towns in the pick-and-roll. James also made plays as a basket defender, including during his pivotal late-game block on Mikal Bridges.

Common sense dictates that James won't play 34 minutes as he did Tuesday -- nor play this much center -- over the long haul of the season. But Game 1 revealed both the role James is willing to play for Philadelphia and a willingness from coach Nick Nurse to get creative right away.

More takeaways from opening night

Point KAT largely absent from Knicks offense

Jalen Brunson shot 6-for-19. Bridges shot 2-for-8. OG Anunoby was 1-from-9 from behind the arc, where New York shot a meager 37% as a team.

Towns had one assist.

When the Knicks swept (a very different) 76ers team in the 2026 playoffs, Towns averaged 7.5 assists per game, as New York's title run relied heavily on his ability as a trigger man at the top of the offense. That was missing from Tuesday's game plan. Early foul trouble played a role, but there is a track record that the more touches Towns gets, the more potent the Knicks' offense can be.

The ball wasn't sticking in Philly's new offense

Other than Tyrese Maxey, who had 28 points, none of the Sixers had a great offensive night; James and Embiid combined to shoot 9-for-28. But the stars followed through with a principle Nurse has instilled since training camp: encourage ball movement.

And that was absolutely working. Embiid and James combined for 13 assists, while Maxey and Jaylen Brown combined for 11.

This is a cornerstone of how the 76ers want and need to play. They have a lot of offensive talent -- Anfernee Simons' 13 points off the bench is part of that -- but to use it they have to share the ball. This, in theory, should make Philadelphia a resilient team this season. It did on opening night.

Rookie Aday Mara instantly impacts the Wemby battle

Over the past year, Victor Wembanyama has given Oklahoma City nightmares game-planning for the team

articles.headline: Saints GM Mickey Loomis asks for patience with 'young developing team'
articles.description: Saints general manager Mickey Loomis said he understands the recent criticism from owner Gayle Benson but asked for patience with what he called a "young developing team."
articles.headlineJa: セインツのGMミッキー・ルーミス、「成長途上の若いチーム」に対し忍耐を求める
articles.descriptionJa: セインツのゼネラルマネージャー、ミッキー・ルーミスは、ゲイル・ベンソンオーナーによる最近の批判については理解を示しつつも、「成長過程にある若いチーム」として忍耐強く見守ってほしいと語った。
articles.body:
VERSAILLES, France -- New Orleans Saints general manager Mickey Loomis said Wednesday he understands the recent criticism from owner Gayle Benson but asked for patience with what he called a "young developing team."

Benson, in comments before the Saints (2-4) beat the New York Giants last Sunday, said Loomis and his staff are responsible for "building a roster capable of sustained success."

The Saints, who haven't been to the playoffs since the 2020 season, practiced in Versailles outside Paris ahead of Sunday's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

"I understood where she's coming from and I think every once in a while we all need to be a little uncomfortable - that's OK," Loomis said at a news conference dominated by questions about Benson's criticism.

Loomis said that yes, he does feel like the Saints are capable of success but that they haven't consistently shown that.

"We haven't done that yet, have we? This is an outcome-based sport, and it's not good enough yet," he said.

When the team was 1-4, Benson said she would "not accept this level of performance."

She said: "Kellen Moore and his coaches are responsible for preparing our players to perform. Mickey Loomis and our football staff are responsible for building a roster capable of sustained success. The players are responsible for their preparation and execution. I am responsible for holding this organization accountable."

The 38-year-old Moore, in his second season as Saints coach, addressed the comments last week: "Mrs. B's great. We all want better results, and that's how this business is."

The Saints then went out to New York and beat the Giants 34-27 before boarding a flight to Paris.

"We're a young team - young developing team and we have to recognize that," Loomis said Wednesday at the training facility of Versailles soccer club. "I recognize that. We've got a young coach, 22 games into his career, and that's where we're at."

Loomis was asked about benchmarks for this season.

"It's a little more subjective, it's not all objective," he said. "It has a lot to do with young players and how they develop, how they perform, how they improve. There's a variety of things, but I'd rather not get into the specifics of that."

articles.headline: Bills' Sam Franklin Jr. suspended one game for spitting; will appeal, per sources
articles.description: Bills defensive back Sam Franklin Jr. was suspended one game for unsportsmanlike conduct that the league said was a spitting incident against the Raiders.
articles.headlineJa: ビルズのサム・フランクリンJr.、唾吐き行為により1試合出場停止。関係者によると控訴する見込み
articles.descriptionJa: ビルズのディフェンシブバック、サム・フランクリンJr.が、レイダースに対する唾吐き行為という非紳士的な行為により、1試合の出場停止処分を受けた。
articles.body:
BUFFALO -- The NFL has suspended another Buffalo Bills defender for a spitting incident in the team's Week 6 game against the Las Vegas Raiders, this time defensive back and special teams captain Sam Franklin Jr.

Per a league announcement, Franklin will be suspended one game without pay because of an incident that occurred with 1:32 remaining in the Bills' 33-30 victory following a successful Raiders extra point. 

Franklin denies the allegation and will appeal, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Mike Garafolo.

Franklin is the second Bills player suspended for spitting at an opponent in Week 6. The NFL has also suspended safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson one game without pay for an altercation earlier in the game wherein Gardner-Johnson spit in the direction of Raiders tight end Brock Bowers.

In both cases, the suspensions are deemed necessary based on NFL bylaws Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1, referring to any act that is "contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship."

Barring a successful appeal, Franklin will miss the Bills' Week 8 game against the Baltimore Ravens. Buffalo is on a bye this week. Any appeal would be heard by Derrick Brooks, Jordy Nelson, Ron Rivera or James Thrash, who are jointly appointed and paid by the NFL and the NFL Players Association.

A seven-year NFL veteran in his second year with the Bills, Franklin has been on the field for more than three quarters of Buffalo's special teams snaps this season, logging six tackles in six games.

Speaking to reporters Monday about the Gardner-Johnson suspension, Bills coach Joe Brady said that there would be no further punishment doled out beyond the league ruling and that while he believes spitting at an opponent crosses a line, he doesn't need all of his players to behave identically to build the winning culture he's aiming for.

articles.headline: Cristiano Ronaldo leads Khvicha Kvaratskhelia tributes after ACL injury
articles.description: Cristiano Ronaldo has sent words of encouragement to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia after the Paris Saint-Germain winger ruptured his anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) against Barcelona.
articles.headlineJa: クリスティアーノ・ロナウド、ACL負傷したクヴィチャ・クヴァラツヘリアへ激励の言葉を送る
articles.descriptionJa: パリ・サンジェルマンのウィング、クヴィチャ・クヴァラツヘリアがバルセロナ戦で前十字靭帯（ACL）を断裂したことを受け、クリスティアーノ・ロナウドが激励のメッセージを送った。
articles.body:
Cristiano Ronaldo has sent words of encouragement to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia after the Paris Saint-Germain winger ruptured his anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) against Barcelona.

PSG confirmed the 25-year-old will have surgery "in the coming days" on his right knee after colliding with Xavi Espart in his side's 4-2 win over Barcelona in the Champions League.

Kvaratskhelia is now likely to miss the rest of the season as he recovers, although no timeline has been given yet.

The Georgia international said in a post on Instagram he would be back "stronger."

"I thought I was prepared for everything, but not, and I realize that God chose me and if I protected the players on another field, I'm ready to go through these months in labor, pain, tears.

"I know I have to come back stronger for my people who always have my back, I won't let you down I promise I won't waste a second. Thank you all for your support see you soon."

Ronaldo commented on the post, saying: "The hardest battles in football are often the ones nobody sees. I know that feeling, Kvara.

- Sources: Barcelona report PSG to UEFA for 'aggressive' tifo

- How Raphinha's latest transformation made him into Barcelona's star striker

- Yamal vs. Mbappé: Which Clásico star has stronger Ballon d'Or claim?

"But never forget what brought you this far, and don't let a difficult moment make you doubt how far you can go. Keep that fire on. Your best is still to come."

Several PSG teammates, including Marquinhos, Ferran Torres, Achraf Hakimi and Désiré Doué also commented on the post.

"Stay strong my brother you will come back stronger, God is with you," Doué said.

articles.headline: Eli Junior Kroupi returns to Bournemouth training, could face Man United
articles.description: Bournemouth have confirmed that Eli Junior Kroupi -- the club's top-scorer last season -- is back in training and could be in contention to face Manchester United on Sunday.
articles.headlineJa: エリ・ジュニア・クルピがボーンマスの練習に復帰、マンU戦に出場する可能性も
articles.descriptionJa: ボーンマスは、昨シーズンのクラブ最多得点者であるエリ・ジュニア・クルピが練習に復帰したことを発表し、日曜日のマンチェスター・ユナイテッド戦に出場する可能性があるとしている。
articles.body:
Bournemouth have confirmed that Eli Junior Kroupi -- the club's top scorer last season -- is back in training and could be in contention to face Manchester United on Sunday.

The French forward underwent surgery for a foot injury in July and has not featured for the club since.

Speaking ahead of the Cherries' Europa League clash with AC Milan, head coach Marco Rose said that Junior Kroupi was back in team training -- but he cannot take part in the match against the Italian giants as he is not part of Bournemouth's Europa League squad.

"Junior is back into team training but not on the UEFA list, but maybe we can have him for some minutes in Manchester," Rose said.

Junior Kroupi scored 13 goals in 35 games across all competitions last season and broke the record for the most goals scored by a teenager in their debut Premier League season.

He has also been nominated for Men's Young Talent of the Year at the upcoming 2026 Ballon d'Or.

- AC Milan back fan boycott over 'excessive' away ticket prices

- Transfer rumors, news: Are Liverpool the favorite to sign Bournemouth's Scott?

- Ruben Amorim still unbeaten in Serie A after Milan win

ESPN revealed in July that Barcelona were exploring a move for Junior Kroupi but nothing materialised.

Bournemouth got their first Premier League win of the season last weekend over Sunderland and will be hoping to use the momentum as they welcome Ruben Amorim's side to the Vitality Stadium.

articles.headline: What it takes to win a Ballon d'Or: Trophies, goals and playing the PR game
articles.description: It's no longer enough to be the best on-field player in order to have a shot at the Ballon d'Or, soccer's top individual prize. You have to make your case in the media, too -- and it takes a lot of work.
articles.headlineJa: バロンドール獲得に必要なもの：トロフィー、ゴール、そしてPR戦略
articles.descriptionJa: サッカー界最高の個人賞であるバロンドールを狙うには、もはやピッチ上で最高の選手であるだけでは不十分だ。メディアを通じて自らの価値をアピールする必要もあり、それには多大な努力を要する。
articles.body:
What does it take to win the men's Ballon d'Or? Regular world-class performances, at least one major trophy during the past 12 months, big goals when it matters most, superstar status and, increasingly, a PR campaign on a par with a presidential election, to name a few.

These are the crucial elements for any player who aspires to claim football's greatest individual honor.

Humility? Not so much.

It is little wonder that football's elite are so desperate to get their hands on one; heading into Monday's ceremony, the competition is as wide open as it's ever been in the modern era, with the end of the Lionel Messi/Cristiano Ronaldo era fast approaching. This year's leading candidates -- Lamine Yamal, Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappé -- have all had superlative seasons, but only one can take the prize.

Trophies are the ultimate currency for the world's top footballers and none come bigger than the Champions League and men's World Cup, but for those at the summit of the game, the honor of winning a Ballon d'Or is everything. It's a combination of ego, commercial value, legacy and the chance to secure a place in the history books.

- Can ESPN predict the Ballon d'Or winners?

- Champions League Power Rankings: Who's No.1?

- Who deserves to win men's award | Women's award

Messi has eight Ballons d'Or and Ronaldo has five of the gold-dipped trophies, made by Parisian jewelry house Mellerio dits Meller. In the days before Messi and Ronaldo's domination of the award, Michel Platini, Johan Cruyff and Marco van Basten were the gold standard with three each. But for Yamal, Kane and Mbappé, winning the Ballon d'Or is no longer just about letting the football do the talking.

"It has become quite unedifying," a representative of a previous Ballon d'Or winner told ESPN. "It seems that the tone of the PR drive this year has been Give me the Ballon d'Or because I've scored lots of goals, but maybe that's because there isn't an obvious standout candidate and the main contenders see this as the best chance they'll have of winning it."

Prior to the voting closing for this year's award on Sept. 28, Yamal, Mbappé and Kane all gave at least two major interviews about their chances of winning the Ballon d'Or.

"You don't give [Ballon d'Or] to ordinary players," Real Madrid and France forward Mbappé told France Football. "You give it to players who are different. I think I did things that were different this year, so I believe I can win it."

Bayern Munich and England striker Kane was similarly robust about his own chances, telling Marca, "I've never liked to talk about myself too much. The only thing I would say is that last season was incredible, on a personal level and as a team.

"It's true that to finish on 73 goals [last season], the second-highest tally in history, speaks for itself."

Barcelona and Spain forward Yamal, who would become the youngest winner at the age of 19 if he tops the vote, suggested that only he or Mbappé would be worthy winners this year. "

articles.headline: AC Milan back fan boycott over 'excessive' away ticket prices
articles.description: - AC Milan came out firmly in support of its fans protesting against excessive away ticket prices, threatening to retaliate against clubs it believes are unfairly charging Rossoneri supporters.
articles.headlineJa: ACミラン、「法外な」アウェーチケット価格を巡るファンのボイコットを支持
articles.descriptionJa: ACミランは、法外なアウェーチケット価格に抗議するファンを全面的に支持すると表明。ロッソネリのサポーターに対し不当な料金を課していると判断されるクラブに対し、報復措置をとる構えを見せている。
articles.body:
MILAN -- AC Milan came out firmly in support of their fans protesting against excessive away ticket prices, threatening to retaliate against clubs they believe are unfairly charging Rossoneri supporters.

Milan fans are boycotting Sunday night's match at Udinese because the home club is charging €65 ($73), more than double the €30 ($34) traveling supporters pay on average at the Bluenergy Stadium.

In a lengthy statement on Wednesday, Milan said they "understand [the fans'] frustration and fully support their position" -- especially as away trips come with many additional costs -- and that fans should be treated the same regardless of which club they follow.

"The global appeal of Italian football depends heavily on the loyalty and passion of supporters of clubs like AC Milan," the club said. "Charging those same fans excessive prices for away games is not only unfair but undermines the unity of the league at a time when Italian football needs to come together to compete against the Premier League and other European leagues.

"Practices like these only deepen divisions between clubs and creates an unhealthy antagonism between big and small teams in Serie A."

Milan said that they would push for a league-wide cap on excessive away ticket prices but, in the meantime, could hit back at clubs they feel are overcharging their fans.

"We are also prepared to introduce a policy of reciprocity: clubs charging our supporters above average ticket pricing should expect their own fans to face higher prices when visiting San Siro, subject to applicable regulations," Milan said.

"Any additional proceeds generated would be donated to Fondazione Milan to support charitable initiatives benefiting local communities."

articles.headline: How Raphinha's latest transformation made him into Barcelona's star striker
articles.description: Before Raphinha became Barcelona's captain and converted into their main striker, he was Premier League battling relegation at Leeds United. It was the making of him.
articles.headlineJa: ラフィニャの最新の変貌が、いかにして彼をバルセロナのスターストライカーへと変えたか
articles.descriptionJa: ラフィニャがバルセロナのキャプテンとなり、メインストライカーに転向する前、彼はリーズ・ユナイテッドでプレミアリーグの降格争いを繰り広げていた。それが彼を成長させた。
articles.body:
Raphinha's career has been characterized by constant change -- first, as he hopped between clubs in Brazil, Portugal, France, England and Spain. Recently, after settling in at Barcelona since 2022, the change has come in a different way: through coaches and his positioning on the pitch.

The Brazil international joined Xavi Hernández's Barça from Leeds United as a right winger, went on to excel on the left flank under Hansi Flick and is now delivering world-class performances this season as a No. 9, scoring 14 goals in 10 games going into Sunday's Clásico against Real Madrid (watch live at 3 p.m. ET on ABC and ESPN+).

It's perhaps no surprise to see him fulfilling so many different roles. Victor Orta, the sporting director who signed him for Leeds back in 2020, even imagined him playing in other positions.

- Yamal vs. Mbappé: Who has the stronger claim to win the Ballon d'Or?

- Tyler, The Creator joins list of music stars to appear on Barça Clásico kit

- Clásico match ball for Barcelona vs. Real Madrid LaLiga clashes unveiled

"I remember one day watching Vitória de Guimarães and thinking he could play as a wing back," Orta tells ESPN. "He had a different style to the typical, technical Brazilian. I said, 'Wow, he looks like he could run the 400 meters in athletics.'"

Raphinha will be 30 in December, and his path to the top of the game has not always been obvious. The 7-year-old who attended Ronaldinho's birthday party was not among the many Brazilian teenagers catapulted straight to one of Europe's elite clubs.

Instead, after fighting his way through várzea tournaments in his homeland -- dubbed by Raphinha himself as "the home of the rejects" -- he landed in Portugal with Vitória, going on to play for Sporting CP and then to French Ligue 1 club Stade Rennais. However, it was at Leeds, in the Premier League spotlight, where his career accelerated. 

Raphinha at Leeds

That is not to say it has been straightforward since. He was not always happy with his game time under former coach Xavi Hernández at Barça and thought he would leave the Spanish champions before Hansi Flick took over in 2024.

In Flick, he has found a manager whose style fits him superbly. The same could be said with Marcelo Bielsa at Leeds, although the Argentine coach wasn't convinced at first.

"Raphinha had been on our radar for a while, but the deal only became possible late in the transfer window," says Orta, now working at Spanish club Real Valladolid. "I was in the barbers one Saturday, very early, and I got a message from someone working with [Raphinha's then-agent, now Barça sporting director] Deco saying: 'Raphinha can leave because a new player is coming in.'

"I remember telling Marcelo. Perhaps because he didn't know him so well, the first reaction was: 'Do you know if he is good? Let me think...'

articles.headline: The Anthony Edwards-LaMelo Ball partnership opens with chemistry and hope
articles.description: The new LaMelo Ball-Anthony Edwards backcourt opens the season with a lot of flash and a renewed joy in Minnesota.
articles.body:
LAMELO BALL LEANS back at the top of the key and hoists the ball toward the rim, his weight on his back feet. He's stoic as the first two fall through the net. He shoots the third as if its swish is a fait accompli.

The ball rims out and he throws his hands on his head and yells, "F---!"

Anthony Edwards stands next to him, laughing. This is his opportunity. He drills three shots in a row with ease, throwing an exaggerated fist bump in the air as the third falls through the hoop. He moves on to the next station.

It's late September, and the first day of training camp for the Minnesota Timberwolves, but most of the team has been practicing together for weeks. The final drill of the day is the classic schoolyard game: Around the World, where a player must hit three shots in a row, circling the 3-point arc. All of the Wolves' guards are competing against one another.

The next time Ball gets his chance, he is standing alone at the top of the key. He's more focused this time. His weight is shifting more toward his toes. He knocks down three in a row.

Ball moves to his right for the next station, hitting the first two and bouncing on his feet as he lets the third go. As it caroms off the rim, Ball walks around the court and pulls his shirt nearly over his head in disbelief.

"A lot of joy," Wolves veteran center Rudy Gobert says as he observes the practice environment. "The vibes are great. I think we needed that."

Despite making the Western Conference finals in two of the past three years, Minnesota overhauled its roster this summer, bringing in Ball to bolster the backcourt alongside Edwards.

It made the Wolves smaller in the process -- trading Julius Randle, their key return in the 2024 Karl-Anthony Towns trade, and fan favorite Naz Reid -- but it also made them younger. Jonathan Kuminga, 24, who was signed in the offseason, and the 26-year-old Ayo Dosunmu are expected to play key roles while fitting in with Edwards' timeline.

They hope the gamble will help them compete with the San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder, the past two conference champions who have used their size to knock out the Wolves in back-to-back playoffs.

"We weren't the best version ourselves last year in the playoffs, but we also know how high the bar is in the Western Conference," Wolves president Tim Connelly said at the team's media day. "We're very aware of what we have to overcome and how difficult that task will be. And we think we're more prepared than ever."

The Wolves recognized their need to lessen Edwards' ballhandling duties, and he has been more than happy to welcome the help.

"I feel like I'm a natural two guard at heart," he said. "I never thought I could develop any point guard skills. I know Finchy [coach Chris Finch] harps on me passing the ball, but now we got LaMelo, so I'm happy."

articles.headline: The five biggest questions still facing Luka and the Lakers
articles.description: After a transformative offseason on the floor and off, there are still massive unanswered questions for this Lakers team.
articles.body:
WITH LESS THAN 30 minutes until tipoff before the Los Angeles Lakers' preseason game against the Golden State Warriors last week, Luka Doncic was the only player on the court.

While both rosters readied themselves in the locker rooms at T-Mobile Arena, Doncic -- given the night off by Lakers coach JJ Redick -- used every bit of the hardwood for a basket-to-basket battle against three of L.A. assistant coaches.

In an exercise designed to tap into the mix of ferociousness and joy that Redick says is the optimal emotional plane for the 27-year-old star, Doncic was not given an inch by Lakers head video coordinator Michael Wexler.

The 5-foot-11 Wexler, a gritty guard who earned a spot on the Pepperdine basketball team, was armed with a foam-covered stick to bat at the arms and prod at the body of the six-time All-Star.

Lakers player development coach Justin Robinson -- standing 6-foot-9 with a sturdy frame, like his "Admiral" dad -- waited for the right time to crowd Doncic with a double team.

And then there was Lakers assistant coach Greg St. Jean, who, though he was technically on Doncic's team in case he needed to pass out of the double to reset the offensive possession, occasionally broke the rules and blitzed Doncic, too.

One trip down, Doncic tried a pull-up 3. The next, he got Wexler and Robinson to bite with a hesitation dribble and blew by them for a lay-in.

On another, he planted himself at the foul line and launched the one-legged fadeaway jumper that fueled the Hall of Fame career of his former Dallas Mavericks teammate Dirk Nowitzki.

After half-a-dozen full-court possessions, Doncic caught his breath and shot 45-foot bombs from the sideline.

When he airballed one, Wexler snickered.

"It's not an easy shot, OK?" Doncic barked back.

After the break, Doncic blazed down the left side of the court and veered back through the lane with a right-hand dribble when Wexler cut him off.

With all of his momentum taking him toward the sideline, Doncic put the ball in his left hand, extended that arm back toward the basket and flipped in a finger roll over Wexler's head, eliciting an "oooohhhh" from the hundreds of fans in the lower bowl.

After the bucket, Doncic flipped his middle finger in front of Wexler's face.

Retribution.

Lakers president of basketball operations and general manager Rob Pelinka watched all of this unfold from the bench, sitting next to Doncic's physiotherapist, Javy Barrio.

If it's the coaches' responsibility to motivate Doncic with creative drills like this 15-minute pregame gauntlet in Las Vegas, it's Barrio's job to keep him healthy, after a late-season hamstring injury sidelined him for the playoffs last spring.

Which leaves Pelinka tasked with building a team around Doncic's spectacular talent -- he secured the second scoring title of his career last season by topping 40 points 16 times -- that can contend for a championship.

articles.headline: Victor Wembanyama, Giannis Antetokounmpo lead record African heritage presence in NBA
articles.description: Eighteen African countries are represented in the league, with Nigeria accounting for nearly half the number with 29 players of Nigerian origin.
articles.headlineJa: ヴィクター・ウェンバンヤマとヤニス・アデトクンボが牽引、NBAでアフリカ系選手の在籍数が過去最多を記録
articles.descriptionJa: リーグにはアフリカ18カ国の出身者が在籍しており、そのうちナイジェリア系選手が29名と、全体の約半分を占めている。
articles.body:
San Antonio Spurs star Victor Wembanyama, Miami Heat teammates Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo, along with Philadelphia 76ers centre Joel Embiid and Washington Wizards rookie AJ Dybantsa, the No. 1 overall draft pick, lead a record 67 players of African origin on opening night rosters for the 2026-27 NBA season.

This year's African presence in the league exceeds the more than 55 players born on the continent or with at least one African parent at the start of last season and comes despite the league's overall international contingent falling to 125 from last season's record 135.

In total, the international players represent 43 countries across six continents, with every NBA team carrying at least one international player.

Eighteen African countries are represented in the league, with Nigeria accounting for nearly half the number with 29 players of Nigerian origin.

Besides Adebayo and Antetokounmpo, Nigeria also has OG Anunoby, who helped the New York Knicks to the title last season, Washington Wizards centre Deandre Ayton, whose father is from Nigeria, along with Precious Achiuwa, Charles Bassey, Adem Bona, Josh Okogie, Felix Okpara and Ugonna Onyenso, with Okpara and Onyenso on two-way contracts.

Senegal is a distant second with six, with Cameroon and Mali tied one behind on five. The Senegalese contingent includes Mouhamed Gueye, Khalifa Diop, Tacko Fall, Ousmane Dieng, Sidy Cissoko and Alex Sarr.

Embiid tops the Cameroon posse, alongside Indiana Pacers forward Pascal Siakam, New Orleans Pelicans centre Yves Missi, Chicago Bulls Noa Essengue and Orlando Magic guard Noah Penda.

The African presence extends across several other national contingents. Leading the line is France, which has 13 players of African heritage out of their total of 17 players, including Wembanyama and Nolan Traoré.

Wembanyama's family roots are in the Democratic Republic of the Congo through his father, Félix, while Traoré is of Ivorian and Malian heritage. France's contingent also includes Wizards teammates Bilal Coulibaly, who has ties to Mali, and Alex Sarr, who is of Senegalese origin.

Elsewhere, Japan's Rui Hachimura is of Benin heritage through his father Zakari Jamil, Germany's Dennis Schroeder is of Gambin heritage and Portugal's Neemias Queta has ties to Guinea-Bissau.

These are record numbers for the NBA. For the 2023-24 season, the league reported 15 players from Africa and another 35 with at least one parent from an African country for a total of 50.

That number went up in the 2024-25 season, with a record-tying 17 players from the continent, along with 35 more with African parentage for a total of 52.

Tuesday's opening-night tripleheader saw five of these African heritage players take to the court, with Embiid recording 13 points, 11 rebounds, six assists and three blocks as Philadelphia beat defending champion New York 106-100.
